correctness.rationale: A selected vertex of layer i sees exactly x_(i+1) selected successors, hence admissibility is x_i=0 or x_(i+1)≤floor(m/2). Empty/nonempty weighted transition M=[[1,(1+z)^m−1],[1,B(z)−1]] counts cyclic layer words exactly once and Cayley–Hamilton yields recurrence. Each heavy layer forces empty predecessor; disjoint pairs bound selected total by floor(dm/2). Equality classifies cyclic matchings, yielding stated leading coefficients. Vertex-transitive averaging gives χ*=dm/floor(dm/2). Two colours are either everywhere balanced for even m or alternate monochromatic layers for even d; otherwise three suffice. Independent exhaustive subset-vs-occupancy comparisons covered 12 small (d,m) instances and their maximum coefficients; finite checks only corroborate unrestricted proof.
